newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Former Command MD sets up oil explorer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Former Command MD sets up oil explorer.

text.p: Former Command Petroleum Holdings NL managing director John Doran has set up a private oil exploration company with a view to an eventual listing.
Doran told Reuters on Thursday that Roc Oil Pty Ltd would spend up to three years searching for suitable projects around the world.

Private backers had contributed search capital, and the company intended to eventually build up a net portfolio of holdings worth A$50-A$100 million. "There is enough money to search and the people who are funding the search would be well
able to fund the acquisitions," he said.
Doran, who will be managing director, said Roc would employ about half a dozen staff and consultants, and look for projects that were "sensibly contrary".
This meant "things that are slightly ugly, things that require a lot of hard work, things where value can be added because the value isn't obvious".
Doran severed his ties with Command this week when he resigned as a director following its takeover by U.K. oil and gas independent Cairn Energy Plc.
Cairn has moved to compulsory acquisition after earlier gaining control of 91.16 percent of the company.
Command's main producing asset is its 22.5 percent operating interest in the Ravva oilfield off the coast of India. Other production interests are spread in Yemen, Tunisia and Russia.
Doran said Roc, named after the legendary bird from the Arabian Nights, would eventually be known as Roc Oil Co Ltd and seek a stock market listing.
However, as a private company, it would be able to search for suitable properties away from the market spotlight.
"We want to be able to judge opportunities on the basis of technical and commercial realities, not on market perceptions," he said.
Doran would not specify the level of search funds available, but said it was more than working capital of some small companies.
A stock market listing could take place at any time from one to four years or longer, he said.
